problem.title: Upgrade Seat Tiers by Utilization Threshold
problem.prompt: You work for an enterprise software vendor tracking seat utilization across customer accounts. Each account has a current tier (Basic, Standard, Premium) and a utilization percentage calculated from active seats divided by total seats. Management wants to upgrade accounts that demonstrate strong adoption: accounts in 'Basic' tier with ≥80% utilization should be upgraded to 'Standard'; accounts in 'Standard' tier with ≥90% utilization should be upgraded to 'Premium'; accounts already in 'Premium' or below the threshold for their tier remain unchanged. Write a single UPDATE statement that applies these tier upgrade rules using a CASE expression in the SET clause. After the update, select all rows ordered by account_id to confirm the final state.

composite_moves: row-transform: conditional tier upgrade based on utilization thresholds

hints: You'll need a CASE expression that checks both the current tier and the utilization percentage to determine the new tier value.
Basic accounts with utilization_pct >= 80 become Standard; Standard accounts with utilization_pct >= 90 become Premium; all others keep their current tier.

Use UPDATE customer_accounts SET tier = CASE WHEN tier = 'Basic' AND utilization_pct >= 80 THEN 'Standard' WHEN tier = 'Standard' AND utilization_pct >= 90 THEN 'Premium' ELSE tier END, then SELECT * FROM customer_accounts ORDER BY account_id.
problem.answer_key:
UPDATE customer_accounts SET tier = CASE WHEN tier = 'Basic' AND utilization_pct >= 80 THEN 'Standard' WHEN tier = 'Standard' AND utilization_pct >= 90 THEN 'Premium' ELSE tier END;
SELECT * FROM customer_accounts ORDER BY account_id;
